newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar extends losses vs mark by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar extends losses vs mark by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0633 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar extended its losses against the mark by late Tokyo on Monday from New York, with the market's focus shifting to German interest rates ahead of the Bundesbank's decision on money market rates on Tuesday.
The dollar was driven down from a high of 118.05 yen on comments by a U.S. trade official, but firm bids by Japanese institutional investors firmly supported the dollar/yen.
Tokyo stocks closed lower following plunges on Wall Street on Friday, with the 225-share Nikkei average falling 284.93 points to close at 19,041.10.
But the impact of the Japanese stock market's fall on dollar/yen trading was limited, dealers said.
"The dollar/yen tested both directions, but the dollar was unable to set a decisive trend in Tokyo," a Japanese commercial bank manager said. "People were looking at the mark."
The smaller-than-expected rise in Japan's trade surplus for July lifted the dollar/yen in early trade on bids by Japanese trust banks and U.S. securities firms, dealers said.

But such an advance was short-lived after remarks by Deputy U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) Jeffrey Lang, who said the United States was concerned about Japan's trade figures. This dragged down the dollar from a high of 118.05 yen.
Asked how concerned the USTR was by the rise in Japan's surplus, Lang told Reuters: "I haven't seen the trade figures this morning, but we are concerned."

The Japanese Finance Ministry said on Monday that the overall customs-cleared surplus climbed 70 percent in July to 849 billion yen, while the surplus with the United States grew 36 percent to nearly 421 billion yen.
Forecasts had been for a rise of from 60 percent to 114 percent in the surplus, or a surplus of 799 billion yen to 1.07 trillion yen.
Dealers said the dollar could face stronger corrective sales attacks against the mark depending on the Bundesbank's decision on interest rates.

The Bundesbank's recent warning of inflationary pressure in Germany and a desire to make a single European currency stable raised expectations that the bank may nudge short-term interest rates higher over the next several weeks.
"The technical sentiment of the dollar/mark will likely deteriorate more rapidly should the dollar fall below 1.8050 marks," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
The German central bank is expected to set the securities repurchase agreements (repo) rate on Tuesday and will hold a council meeting on Thursday after a four-week summer break.

"Even if the Bundesbank decides to leave its interest rates unchanged, the mark could be supported as long as speculation of an interest rate hike lingers in the market," the dealer said. The dollar closed at 117.39/44 yen and 1.8185/95 marks in New York on Friday.-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
